final_recommendation: The room converged on a narrow labor-enforcement amendment with automatic U.S. tariff suspension triggered by panel ruling, 70% regional wage floor, and independent union registration timelines in primary text. Democrats commit to floor vote Wednesday/Thursday contingent on labor sign-off Friday; Canada secured written assurance dairy and Chapter 19 remain untouched.
minority_objections: Labor union initially demanded unilateral U.S. enforcement authority without bilateral panel, rejected as sovereignty violation by Mexico
Mexico resisted naming specific wage floors in primary text until final rounds, citing domestic sovereignty concerns
key_conflicts: Labor vs. Mexico on enforcement mechanism: unilateral U.S. action vs. bilateral panel with automatic triggers
Specificity of wage floors and union timelines: primary treaty text vs. side letters
Implementation authority: whether Mexico executes panel remedies or U.S. tariff suspension is automatic and unilateral
key_concessions: Mexico accepted 70% wage floor and union registration timelines in primary amendment text
Labor accepted bilateral panel mechanism instead of unilateral U.S. enforcement, contingent on automatic tariff suspension
Democrats committed to narrow amendment scope, leaving dairy and Chapter 19 untouched per Canada's demand
Business accepted amendment reopening in exchange for tight drafting timeline and floor-vote commitment
red_lines: Labor: no side letters for wage floors or union timelines; must be in primary text with no ambiguity
Mexico: no U.S. interference in domestic labor courts; tariff suspension must be unilateral U.S. action, not Mexican implementation
Canada: no reopening of dairy concessions or Chapter 19 dispute resolution
Democrats: automatic tariff suspension with no discretionary 'Mexico implements' language
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Media framing risk: whether automatic tariff suspension reads as 'labor victory' or 'U.S. sovereignty violation over Mexico' remained unresolved until final rounds
Timeline risk: Friday sign-off to Monday circulation to Wednesday floor vote is extremely compressed; any drafting gap could collapse the deal
Mexican domestic ratification: room assumed Mexico's Congress would accept the amendment, but no explicit confirmation of Mexican legislative timeline or support
Business mobilization contingency: business lobby conditioned support on certainty but did not specify fallback if floor vote slips past Thursday
downstream_risk_variables: Labor sign-off Friday night on final draft language
Mexican Congress acceptance of primary-text wage floors and union timelines
Media narrative Monday-Wednesday: 'enforcement with teeth' vs. 'U.S. overreach'
Democratic caucus unity on floor vote Wednesday/Thursday
Canada's ability to defend narrow amendment scope domestically without reopening dairy
uncertainty_notes: Room achieved procedural convergence on amendment text and floor-vote timeline, but three critical uncertainties remain unresolved: (1) whether labor will actually sign off Friday if any drafting ambiguity surfaces, (2) whether Mexico's domestic politics can absorb the primary-text commitments without sovereignty backlash, and (3) whether the compressed timeline (draft Friday, circulate Monday, vote Wednesday) leaves enough space for unforeseen legal or political gaps to surface and be resolved.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Democrats explicitly stated 'if my members see vague language Monday, we're reopening this' and conditioned floor vote on labor sign-off; ratification failure drove every round's urgency and shaped all concessions.
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: Labor's demand for primary-text wage floors, automatic panel triggers, and no side letters dominated R1-R5; room restructured entire amendment around labor's three non-negotiables (10-day panel, no veto, mandatory suspension).
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Business conditioned support on tight drafting timeline and floor-vote commitment, but did not drive the room's direction; accepted amendment reopening as necessary compromise rather than shaping its substance.
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Canada secured written assurance that dairy and Chapter 19 remain untouched, which stabilized the amendment's scope, but this was a defensive red line rather than a driving force in the labor-enforcement debate.
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Mexico's insistence that tariff suspension be unilateral U.S. action (not Mexican implementation) and that domestic labor courts remain sovereign shaped the final legal language in R4-R5; sovereignty concern was a central constraint throughout.
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Media actor repeatedly pressed for clarity on headline framing ('enforcement with teeth' vs. 'U.S. overreach'), and labor's press strategy was discussed, but media pressure was a secondary consideration rather than a primary driver of substantive decisions.
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Room treated amendment as necessary to unlock ratification; Democrats stated 'we're reopening this' if language fails, and all parties structured concessions around the assumption that the package cannot pass as-is without labor enforcement amendment.
